[RDSC.8.7] **Side condition — cross-atom referential integrity.** [RDSC.8.1]
admits a well-formed atom sequence whose atoms name things no other atom
defines. Each of these is a well-formedness condition over the parsed stream,
not over the production set.

- A `Hydration` atom names a slot that a `Slot` atom in the same file declares
  ([RDSC.5.6.4]), and at most one `Hydration` exists per `(schema, slot)`
  ([RDSC.5.6.5]).
- A `rule_group`'s atoms name a rule that a `TerminalNode` atom realizes ([RDSC.8.3]).
- An `AlphaNode` atom names a schema that some `schema_group` registers.
- An `oracle_atom`, and every test atom but `TestCase` and `TestReply`, names
  the `TestCase` test it belongs to; a `TestReply` names the `TestResponse`
  stub it answers.

Note that the first three of these are satisfied **across** the bundle-global
boundary: a `rule_group` is emitted inside its `module_group`, while the `TerminalNode`
atom realizing its rule arrives later, in `rete_network`. The reference is by
name, resolved once the whole artefact is read, never by position.

A loader **must** refuse an artefact in which an atom it reads names something
that no atom in the artefact defines, as listed above, with `DS_ERR_DSC_DANGLING`
([RDSC.11.1]). The artefact alone decides.

**The stream is parsed when every atom body is decoded in full:** its protobuf decode ([RDSC.9.5]), and the shape a network
node's own clause gives it, which covers a node id ([RDSC.4a.3]), an `AlphaNode`'s
schema name ([RDSC.4a.6.3]) and an expression's shape ([RDSC.11.3]). A loader
**must** refuse a body that fails any of these before it checks a name this
clause lists, so an artefact with both defects is refused for the body. A check
that needs the registered schemas is not part of decoding a body.

**The last bullet binds the reader of test atoms, not a runtime's loader.**
A runtime skips the test and oracle atoms ([RDSC.7.6], [RTIM.8.3.1]),
and [RDSC.9.9] forbids it to analyse what its load does not use, so it does not
check what they name. The `.dstest` interpreter reads them, and it **must**
refuse the run, running no case, over a test atom that names a test or a stub
no atom declares ([RTIM.14.15]).
